connection_condition: member.link_to_major corresponds to major.major_id; one of the 33 members has no linked major
description: A member is enrolled in at most one major. This is a reference from member to major, not a type-of or part-of relation.

connection_condition: major.department and major.college co-occur on the same major row; every department maps to exactly one college
description: A college is composed of departments; every academic department belongs to exactly one college.

connection_condition: each major row carries the department that offers it; a major belongs to exactly one department
description: A department is composed of the majors it offers; each major belongs to exactly one department.
An event is composed of its budget lines; a budget line cannot exist without an event, and every budget line links to exactly one event.
A budget line is composed of the expense records charged against it; every expense links to exactly one budget line.
An expense is attributed to the member who incurred it; the expense record identifies its member.
Income records such as dues are attributed to the member they were received from.
An attendance record belongs to one member; it cannot exist without that member.
An attendance record belongs to one event; it cannot exist without that event.
A member's full name is derived by joining the member's first name and last name with a single space.

connection_condition: the leading four characters of event.event_date
description: The event year is derived from the year portion of the event date string.

connection_condition: sum of expense.cost grouped by expense.link_to_budget equals budget.spent for the same budget line
description: The amount spent on a budget line is derived as the total cost of the expenses charged against that budget line; the two agree for all 52 budget lines with no mismatch.

connection_condition: budget.event_status equals event.status for all 52 budget lines joined to their event
description: The status carried on a budget line expresses the same business concept as the event's own status, so either column can represent event status.

Budget categories (Food, Parking, Speaker Gifts, ...) and event types (Meeting, Guest Speaker, ...) are two different classification axes that both describe club activity and frequently co-occur, but no direct structural link exists between them.

connection_condition: both are monetary columns of the same budget row (budget.amount and budget.spent)
description: Budgeted amount and amount spent are two monetary measures of the same budget line. They are related but distinct measures and must not be treated as equivalent.

connection_condition: income.link_to_member corresponds to member.member_id, so per-member income can be traced to its source
description: Income sources such as dues are recorded against individual members, linking the source of funds to the member who provided them.
